prompt:
Edit the supplied Korean building artwork into a NEW companion UPGRADE SPRITE SHEET for the same game. Reference image 1 (tower-tiers-v2.webp) is the exact approved style/camera/material/lighting and small-scale game sprite rendering to match. Reference image 2 (buildings.webp) supplies the FOUR landmark identities described below. Do not reproduce the original sheet layout. Output one precise FIVE COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS atlas, 20 equally sized SQUARE cells, overall 5:4 landscape ratio, actual alpha transparent background. Every cell contains ONE isolated complete building, no text or UI.

Art direction: beautiful richly painted premium animated-film Korean historical fantasy game assets, softly rounded weathered granite, detailed carved wood, elegant blue-black curved Korean roof tiles, restrained deep-red lacquer pillars, muted green dancheong, antique gold details and warm amber lantern windows. Same elevated three-quarter orthographic game camera in every cell, looking down about 45 degrees. Warm upper-left key with cool blue fill; all surfaces retain shaded volume. Preserve believable Korean architecture and the identities in the reference. NO noisy procedural grain, hard black outline, flat low-poly style, neon, photorealistic photo, scene background, shadow puddle, people, lettering, watermark, gridlines or labels.

Critical composition: five equal-width columns, four equal-height rows. Each object fully contained within CENTRAL 76 percent of its square cell with at least 12 percent completely transparent margin on ALL sides. All FIVE versions of each row have IDENTICAL overall height, IDENTICAL compact ground footprint and same baseline. Upgrading changes materials, roof details, visible equipment, shrine facade and small decorations within that existing footprint; NEVER make later tiers taller, broader, more storeys, a larger base or sprawl. The first THREE columns must be clearly different even as small sprites. Columns 4 and 5 are equally finished, visually different specializations, not bigger versions. Base on low stone plinths with visible contact detail but no cast ground shadow and no terrain patches outside the plinth.

Exact ordering, left to right:
ROW 1 — BOSINGAK Korean bell pavilion (reference building row1 col3): open four red pillars, dark blue tiled roof, a bronze hanging bell visibly centered.
1 simple stone plinth, plain wooden posts and small undecorated bronze bell.
2 reinforced red lacquer posts, carved brackets, bronze bell with clear relief bands, two restrained amber lanterns.
3 polished deep bronze bell, elaborate mint-gold dancheong beamwork, bronze roof-end ornaments, richer carved railing, same single roof size.
4 EMILLE specialization: monumental-looking engraved gold-bronze ceremonial bell inside the SAME pavilion, two small golden resonator disks beside bell, antique gold roof details and small crimson cloth pennants.
5 CURFEW specialization: dark patinated bronze bell, paired compact hanging signaling drums beside it, dark navy cloth pennants and pale jade roof accents.

ROW 2 — CHEOMSEONGDAE Korean stone observatory (reference row1 col4): characteristic tapered bottle-shaped round granite tower, square opening in side and square stone rim at top. NO fantasy castle turret or roof.
1 aged plain granite courses, dark central window, plain square top rim.
2 neatly reinforced stone base bands, pale bronze aperture frame, small brass observation instrument visible at rim.
3 finished precision stone courses and bronze rings around upper neck, intricate brass star chart wheel inset beside aperture, tiny warm celestial light in window.
4 ARMILLARY specialization: a compact ornate antique-brass armillary sphere nested within top rim, warm gold aperture and circular astral engraving; sphere kept WITHIN the SAME height envelope.
5 ROYAL OBSERVATION specialization: a compact dark navy brass sighting telescope and jade star map equipment nested at top rim, cool pale cyan window and two small navy pennants; same total height.

ROW 3 — HAEINSA scripture repository (reference row2 col1): broad single-storey Korean timber scripture hall, visible wooden slatted lattice windows, dark tiled gable roof, modest raised granite base.
1 plain dark timber lattice, simple stone footing, restrained amber doorway.
2 deep-red framed lattice and short carved porch railing, reinforced plinth, two amber lanterns.
3 elegant green-and-gold dancheong brackets, visible ranks of warm wooden scripture blocks behind lattice, detailed ridge ends and carved stone steps, same roof/footprint.
4 SCRIPTURE WARD specialization: visible bronze-framed racks of sutra wooden blocks at the open front, subtle engraved gold circle on central panel, gold-green roof details and compact deep-red streamers.
5 PROTECTIVE RITE specialization: welcoming amber-lit open ceremonial entry, two small jade/brass incense bowls and muted green fabric canopies tucked under existing eaves, richer carved lattice and jade roof ends.

ROW 4 — SEOKGURAM stone Buddha grotto (reference row2 col2): compact rounded granite grotto shell and clearly visible seated golden Buddha in central arched entry; one coherent shrine, not an outdoor building with added roof.
1 rough mossy round stone mound, simple arch, small warmly lit seated Buddha.
2 dressed granite arch blocks, carved short stone steps, two small stone lanterns, same mound size.
3 richly carved finished arch and lotus-pattern stonework, detailed seated Buddha and antique-gold lotus halo inside arch, tidy sparse moss.
4 GREAT RADIANCE specialization: large ornate GOLD sun halo tightly behind the same seated Buddha, etched warm golden arch bands and central focused amber light, all confined inside original grotto silhouette.
5 THOUSAND-BUDDHA specialization: three small visible gold Buddha figures within the same arch chamber, several small jade-and-gold lotus halos and cool pale jade arch inlay; no huge glow outside building.

Do not add snow. These compact buildings must work in spring, summer, autumn and winter. Transparent alpha pixels between and around all objects. Highest practical detail and clean antialiased silhouette, readable as tiny real gameplay sprites.
runtime: Explicit transparent-cell boundaries; isolated padded CanvasTextures; fixed 1.2 world-unit height.
